topic: 2025-2026 viability context: UN snapback sanctions and the 2026 Iran war
wiki_text: The Iran LNG (NIOC LNG) project at Tombak Port was reported roughly 50-53% physically complete after its 2021-2023 revival, with Iran's oil ministry targeting an initial 1.5 mtpa 'Train 3' medium-sized plant for 2026 and a longer-term total of up to 20 mtpa (Argus, January 2024; OGJ). Two developments after September 2025 have sharply reduced the project's near-term viability. First, the United Nations 'snapback' sanctions mechanism was triggered by France, Germany and the United Kingdom on 28 August 2025 and the pre-2015 UN sanctions regime was formally reimposed on 28 September 2025, further restricting Iran's access to liquefaction technology and international finance. Second, the 2026 Iran war (US- and Israeli-led strikes beginning in late February 2026) and Iran's closure of the Strait of Hormuz on 4 March 2026 stranded regional oil and LNG exports and damaged Gulf LNG infrastructure, including Qatar's Ras Laffan complex. No source documents a formal halt to construction at the Tombak site, but the project's stated 2026 commissioning target is widely regarded as unrealistic given long-standing sanctions, an estimated US$10 billion funding gap, missing liquefaction technology, and the post-2025 escalation.
